verdict.rationale: BugSnag documents its own rule-based automations that run in the background without user action. Automatic error-assignment rules route errors to teams or collaborators. Integrations act on incoming errors on their own: PagerDuty creates incidents, and the webhook plugin forwards event data to a URL. These automations are narrow, event-triggered triage and forwarding behaviours, not general user-defined or agentic workflows. missing for 10: general-purpose configurable automation or workflow builder, scheduled or recurring jobs, AI or agent-driven autonomous actions, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Triaging errors can be a repetitive process... BugSnag allows you to create rules to automate this process.
assigning all errors that originate from files in the src/components/cart directory to the “Cart Team” or an individual collaborator. BugSnag allows you to create rules to automate this process.
The PagerDuty integration creates incidents in PagerDuty when error activity is reported to BugSnag.
The plugin sends a message to the specified URL containing information about the event, error, project and account.
